title: 06. Playwright Basics, Locators & Waiting: Keyboard operations & Reading element information
summary: Use a locator-specific keyboard operation when the target element is known. Use page-level keyboard operations when interacting with the currently focused control or simulating broader keyboard sequences.

sections.title: Keyboard operations
sections.body:
Use a locator-specific keyboard operation when the target element is known.

Use page-level keyboard operations when interacting with the currently focused control or simulating broader keyboard sequences.

## 15.1 Common keyboard keys

| Key | Example |
|--------|--------|
| Enter | Submit or confirm |
| Tab | Move focus |
| Shift+Tab | Move focus backward |
| Escape | Close dialog or dismiss popup |
| ArrowDown | Navigate options |
| ArrowUp | Navigate options |
| Backspace | Remove preceding character |
| Delete | Delete selected or following content |
| ControlOrMeta+A | Select all |

## 15.2 Python

```python
page.get_by_label("Question").focus()

page.keyboard.insert_text(
    "Explain vector databases"
)

page.keyboard.press("Enter")
```

## 15.3 TypeScript

```typescript
await page.getByLabel("Question").focus();

await page.keyboard.insertText(
    "Explain vector databases"
);

await page.keyboard.press("Enter");
```

This assumes the chatbot implements Enter as a submission shortcut. A multiline textarea may otherwise insert a newline.

## 15.4 Keyboard accessibility testing

Python:

```python
page.get_by_label("Email").focus()

page.keyboard.press("Tab")

expect(
    page.get_by_label("Password")
).to_be_focused()
```

TypeScript:

```typescript
await page.getByLabel("Email").focus();

await page.keyboard.press("Tab");

await expect(

    page.getByLabel("Password")

).toBeFocused();
```

This verifies an expected tab order, which is important for keyboard accessibility.

sections.title: Mouse operations
sections.body:
## 16.1 Locator interaction vs coordinate interaction

Preferred for ordinary UI controls:

```typescript
await page.getByRole("button", {
    name: "Send"
}).click();
```

Coordinate-based interaction:

```typescript
await page.mouse.click(200, 300);
```

The second method uses viewport coordinates rather than semantic element identification.

Coordinate interactions are useful for canvases, diagram editors, drawing applications and specialized graphical interfaces.

They are generally more sensitive to layout, scroll position and viewport changes.

## 16.2 Common mouse operations

| Operation | Python | TypeScript |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Move | `page.mouse.move(x, y)` | `await page.mouse.move(x, y)` |
| Click | `page.mouse.click(x, y)` | `await page.mouse.click(x, y)` |
| Double-click | `page.mouse.dblclick(x, y)` | `await page.mouse.dblclick(x, y)` |
| Press button | `page.mouse.down()` | `await page.mouse.down()` |
| Release button | `page.mouse.up()` | `await page.mouse.up()` |
| Scroll | `page.mouse.wheel(dx, dy)` | `await page.mouse.wheel(dx, dy)` |

## 16.3 Drag and drop

Suppose you are testing a visual multi-agent workflow builder.

There is a Research Agent node that must be dragged into a workflow area.

Python:

```python
source = page.get_by_test_id(
    "research-agent"
)

target = page.get_by_test_id(
    "workflow-canvas"
)

source.drag_to(target)
```

TypeScript:

```typescript
const source = page.getByTestId(
    "research-agent"
);

const target = page.getByTestId(
    "workflow-canvas"
);

await source.dragTo(target);
```

sections.title: Checkboxes and radio buttons
sections.body:
## 17.1 Checkboxes

Checkboxes represent independent Boolean selections.

For example, an AI chatbot may allow users to enable citations, streaming and conversation memory independently.

HTML:

```html
<label>
    <input type="checkbox" />
    Include citations
</label>

<label>
    <input type="checkbox" />
    Enable streaming
</label>
```

Python:

```python
citations = page.get_by_role(

    "checkbox",

    name="Include citations"
)

citations.check()

expect(citations).to_be_checked()

citations.uncheck()

expect(citations).not_to_be_checked()
```

TypeScript:

```typescript
const citations = page.getByRole(

    "checkbox",

    { name: "Include citations" }
);

await citations.check();

await expect(citations).toBeChecked();

await citations.uncheck();

await expect(citations).not.toBeChecked();
```

## 17.2 check() vs click()

Suppose a checkbox is already checked.

```typescript
await checkbox.click();
```

This may toggle it off.

```typescript
await checkbox.check();
```

This ensures the target is checked. An already checked native checkbox normally requires no additional click.

Use `check()` when the required final state matters.

You can also specify a Boolean state directly.

Python:

```python
checkbox.set_checked(True)
```

TypeScript:

```typescript
await checkbox.setChecked(true);
```

## 17.3 Radio buttons

Radio buttons within the same group usually represent mutually exclusive choices.

HTML:

```html
<label>
    <input
        type="radio"
        name="model"
        value="fast"
    />
    Fast model
</label>

<label>
    <input
        type="radio"
        name="model"
        value="reasoning"
    />
    Reasoning model
</label>
```

Python:

```python
page.get_by_role(

    "radio",

    name="Reasoning model"

).check()

expect(

    page.get_by_role(
        "radio",
        name="Fast model"
    )

).not_to_be_checked()
```

TypeScript:

```typescript
await page.getByRole("radio", {

    name: "Reasoning model"

}).check();

await expect(

    page.getByRole("radio", {
        name: "Fast model"
    })

).not.toBeChecked();
```

## 17.4 Interactive AI configuration form

## AI model configuration

Independent capabilities — checkboxes

Equivalent TypeScript interactions

await page.getByRole("checkbox", { name: "Enable streaming" }).setChecked();

For custom components that merely imitate a checkbox or radio button, you may need ordinary click interactions and assertions against their accessible state rather than assuming native input methods apply.

sections.title: Dropdowns — Native vs custom dropdowns
sections.body:
This is a frequent Playwright coding interview topic. ## 18.1 Native HTML dropdown ```html ``` A native dropdown is implemented using an HTML `select` element. ## 18.2 Select by value Python: ```python page.get_by_label( "Select model" ).select_option( value="reasoning" ) ``` TypeScript: ```typescript await page.getByLabel( "Select model" ).selectOption({ value: "reasoning" }); ``` ## 18.3 Select by visible label Python: ```python page.get_by_label( "Select model" ).select_option( label="Reasoning model" ) ``` TypeScript: ```typescript await page.getByLabel( "Select model" ).selectOption({ label: "Reasoning model" }); ``` ## 18.4 Select by index Python: ```python page.get_by_label( "Select model" ).select_option(index=1) ``` TypeScript: ```typescript await page.getByLabel( "Select model" ).selectOption({ index: 1 }); ``` Index selection is zero-based and can become fragile if options are reordered. ## 18.5 Verify selected value Python: ```python expect( page.get_by_label("Select model") ).to_have_value("reasoning") ``` TypeScript: ```typescript await expect( page.getByLabel("Select model") ).toHaveValue("reasoning"); ``` ## 18.6 Multiple-selection dropdown HTML: ```html ``` Python: ```python page.get_by_label( "Enabled tools" ).select_option([ "search", "browser" ]) ``` TypeScript: ```typescript await page.getByLabel( "Enabled tools" ).selectOption([ "search", "browser" ]); ``` The select-option APIs are intended for actual HTML select controls. ## 18.7 Custom dropdowns: React, Material UI and other frontend libraries Many modern applications implement dropdowns using combinations of buttons, divs, ARIA roles and popup lists. Conceptually: ```html
  • Fast model
  • Reasoning model
``` Calling `selectOption()` on that combobox button would fail because it is not an HTML select element. Instead, interact with the custom dropdown as a user would. Python: ```python page.get_by_role( "combobox", name="Select model" ).click() page.get_by_role( "option", name="Reasoning model" ).click() ``` TypeScript: ```typescript await page.getByRole("combobox", { name: "Select model" }).click(); await page.getByRole("option", { name: "Reasoning model" }).click(); ``` The exact roles depend on the frontend component. Inspect the actual DOM and accessibility properties rather than assuming every custom dropdown uses the same structure. ## 18.8 Interactive dropdown laboratory ## Native versus custom dropdown - Native HTML - Custom React UI Select model TypeScript automation Both controls provide a similar user experience but require different automation methods.

sections.title: Reading element information
sections.body:
Before or after interacting with elements, you may need to retrieve their properties. ## 19.1 Common extraction methods | Requirement | Python | TypeScript | |--------|--------|--------| | Rendered inner text | `locator.inner_text()` | `await locator.innerText()` | | DOM text content | `locator.text_content()` | `await locator.textContent()` | | Input value | `locator.input_value()` | `await locator.inputValue()` | | Attribute value | `locator.get_attribute("href")` | `await locator.getAttribute("href")` | | Visibility snapshot | `locator.is_visible()` | `await locator.isVisible()` | | Enabled state | `locator.is_enabled()` | `await locator.isEnabled()` | | Checked state | `locator.is_checked()` | `await locator.isChecked()` | | Matching count | `locator.count()` | `await locator.count()` | | All matched inner texts | `locator.all_inner_texts()` | `await locator.allInnerTexts()` | ## 19.2 innerText vs textContent Consider: ```html
RAG explanation Internal metadata
``` `innerText` generally reflects rendered human-readable text, while `textContent` reflects DOM text, including text in hidden descendants. Python: ```python answer = page.locator("#answer") print(answer.inner_text()) print(answer.text_content()) ``` TypeScript: ```typescript const answer = page.locator("#answer"); console.log(await answer.innerText()); console.log(await answer.textContent()); ``` ## 19.3 Read an input value An input element generally stores its entered content in its value property rather than as child text. Python: ```python value = page.get_by_label( "Question" ).input_value() ``` TypeScript: ```typescript const value = await page.getByLabel( "Question" ).inputValue(); ``` Do not use `innerText()` to retrieve ordinary input values. ## 19.4 Read citation links from a RAG chatbot HTML: ```html
RAG Documentation Agent Guide
``` Python: ```python citations = page.get_by_role( "region", name="Citations" ).get_by_role("link") expect(citations).to_have_count(2) for citation in citations.all(): print({ "title": citation.inner_text(), "href": citation.get_attribute("href") }) ``` TypeScript: ```typescript const citations = page.getByRole("region", { name: "Citations" }).getByRole("link"); await expect(citations).toHaveCount(2); for (const citation of await citations.all()) { console.log({ title: await citation.innerText(), href: await citation.getAttribute("href") }); } ``` This can verify citation presentation and extract citation metadata for additional RAG evaluation. It does not establish whether the cited documents support the generated claims.
